instruction: Kitchen Cabinet Layout Along a 3 m Wall Using SketchUp, lay out a run of 8 kitchen cabinets against a 3 m wall and export it as COLLADA DAE. No initial file is provided. Geometry convention: the wall is the plane Y = 0 and cabinets extend outward in the +Y direction; the floor is Z = 0. The 3 m wall spans X in [0, 3] m. Specification: - **Base row** (4 cabinets, sitting on the floor, 600 mm deep, 900 mm tall): - Widths, left-to-right: 600 mm, 900 mm, 600 mm, 900 mm (total 3 m). - Each base cabinet spans Y in [0, 0.6] m and Z in [0, 0.9] m. - Cumulative X edges: 0 -> 600 -> 1500 -> 2100 -> 3000 mm. - **Wall row** (4 cabinets, hung from the wall, 300 mm deep, 900 mm tall): - Widths, left-to-right: 600 mm each (total 2.4 m, starting flush at the left end of the wall). - Each wall cabinet spans Y in [0, 0.3] m and Z in [1.5, 2.4] m (i.e. the bottom of the wall cabinets is 600 mm above the top of the base cabinets). - Cumulative X edges: 0 -> 600 -> 1200 -> 1800 -> 2400 mm. - **Distinct cabinets**: model the 8 cabinets as 8 distinct components (each with its own per-cabinet box dimensions - they are *not* all identical). Export as `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae`. Requirements: 1. `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae` parses as valid COLLADA. 2. Exactly 8 cabinet instances are present in the scene graph. 3. The 4 base cabinets together span Z in [0, 0.9] m (within 5 mm) and their X ranges tile the cumulative edges {0, 600, 1500, 2100, 3000} mm. Each base cabinet is 600 mm deep along Y. 4. The 4 wall cabinets together span Z in [1.5, 2.4] m (within 5 mm) and their X ranges tile the cumulative edges {0, 600, 1200, 1800, 2400} mm (uniform 600 mm each). Each wall cabinet is 300 mm deep along Y.

command: import pyautogui; import time; RATIO_X = 0.455; RATIO_Y = 0.606; screen_w, screen_h = pyautogui.size(); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click(int(screen_w * RATIO_X), int(screen_h * RATIO_Y))
